events.title: The Creation of the World
events.description: God creates the heavens, the earth, and all life, culminating in the creation of humanity.

events.title: The Fall of Man
events.description: Adam and Eve disobey God in the Garden of Eden, bringing sin and death into the world.

events.title: Cain and Abel
events.description: The first murder in human history, where Cain kills his brother Abel out of jealousy.

events.title: The Flood and Noah's Ark
events.description: God sends a global flood to judge the corruption of humanity, saving only Noah, his family, and the animals in the Ark.

events.title: The Tower of Babel
events.description: Humanity attempts to build a tower to reach the heavens; God confuses their languages and scatters them across the earth.

events.title: The Call of Abraham
events.description: God calls Abraham to leave Ur, promising to make him a great nation and to bless all families of the earth through him.

events.title: The Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah
events.description: God destroys the corrupt cities with fire and brimstone; Lot and his daughters escape, but his wife looks back.

events.title: The Testing of Abraham
events.description: God tests Abraham's faith by asking him to sacrifice Isaac, but provides a ram as a substitute.

events.title: Jacob Deceives Esau
events.description: Jacob acquires his brother Esau's birthright blessing and flees to Paddan-Aram.

events.title: Jacob Wrestles with the Angel
events.description: At the ford of Jabbok, Jacob wrestles all night with God and his name is changed to Israel.

events.title: Joseph in Egypt
events.description: Joseph is sold as a slave, but through divine providence becomes governor and saves his family from famine.

events.title: The Birth of Moses
events.description: Moses is born amidst Hebrew slavery, saved from the waters of the Nile, and raised in Pharaoh's palace.

events.title: The Ten Plagues and the Exodus
events.description: After the plagues on Egypt and the first Passover, Moses leads the people of Israel across the Red Sea.

events.title: The Law at Mount Sinai
events.description: God gives Moses the Ten Commandments and the instructions for building the Tabernacle.

events.title: The Bronze Serpent
events.description: The people are healed from venomous snake bites in the wilderness by looking at a bronze serpent made by Moses.

events.title: The Death of Moses
events.description: Moses views the Promised Land from the top of Mount Nebo and dies before crossing the Jordan.

events.title: The Fall of Jericho
events.description: Led by Joshua, the Israelites enter the Promised Land and the walls of Jericho fall by the power of God.

events.title: The Victory of Deborah
events.description: The prophetess and judge Deborah guides Barak to a great military victory against the Canaanite oppressor Sisera.

events.title: The Victory of Gideon
events.description: Gideon, called by God, defeats the massive Midianite army with only 300 men.

events.title: The Story of Ruth
events.description: Ruth demonstrates loyalty to Naomi and finds redemption with Boaz, becoming an ancestor of King David.

events.title: The Call of Samuel
events.description: Still a boy, Samuel hears the voice of God in the Tabernacle, marking the end of the era of the Judges.

events.title: The Fall of Samson
events.description: Samson destroys the temple of Dagon in his final act of strength against the Philistines.

events.title: Saul Crowned King
events.description: Samuel anoints Saul as the first king of Israel after the people demanded a monarch.

events.title: David and Goliath
events.description: The young shepherd David defeats the Philistine giant Goliath with a sling and a stone.

events.title: David Becomes King and the Covenant
events.description: David assumes the throne of all Israel and God establishes an everlasting covenant with his descendants.

events.title: Solomon's Temple
events.description: Solomon completes the majestic First Temple in Jerusalem and the glory of the Lord fills the place.

events.title: The Visit of the Queen of Sheba
events.description: The queen travels from afar to test Solomon's immense wisdom and is amazed by the glory of his kingdom.

events.title: The Division of the Kingdom
events.description: After Solomon's death, the kingdom divides: Israel (North) under Jeroboam and Judah (South) under Rehoboam.

events.title: Elijah at Mount Carmel
events.description: The prophet Elijah challenges and defeats the prophets of Baal, bringing down fire from heaven.

events.title: The Fall of Israel
events.description: The Assyrian Empire conquers Samaria and takes the ten northern tribes into exile.

events.title: The Reform of King Josiah
events.description: The Book of the Law is found in the Temple, leading King Josiah to initiate a deep spiritual purification in Judah.

events.title: The Fiery Furnace
events.description: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego are thrown into the furnace by Nebuchadnezzar, but emerge unharmed, protected by God.

events.title: Fall of Jerusalem
events.description: The Babylonians destroy Jerusalem and Solomon's Temple, taking the people of Judah into captivity.

events.title: The Vision of the Valley of Dry Bones
events.description: The prophet Ezekiel has a mystical vision of resurrecting bones, symbolizing the future restoration of Israel.

events.title: Daniel in the Lions' Den
events.description: During the Medo-Persian rule, Daniel is thrown to the lions for his faith and is miraculously saved.

events.title: The Decree of Cyrus
events.description: Cyrus, king of Persia, allows the exiled Jews to return to Jerusalem.

events.title: The Completion of the Second Temple
events.description: The new temple is finished in Jerusalem under the leadership of Zerubbabel.

events.title: Esther Saves the Jewish People
events.description: Queen Esther risks her own life to thwart Haman's plot of genocide.

events.title: The Rebuilding of the Walls
events.description: Nehemiah leads the rapid rebuilding of the walls of Jerusalem in just 52 days.

events.title: The Birth of Jesus
events.description: Jesus is born in Bethlehem of Judea, fulfilling messianic prophecies, and is visited by shepherds and wise men.

events.title: The Flight to Egypt
events.description: Warned by an angel, Joseph flees with Mary and the child Jesus to Egypt, escaping the massacre ordered by Herod.

events.title: The Baptism of Jesus
events.description: Jesus is baptized by John the Baptist in the Jordan River, and the Holy Spirit descends upon Him like a dove.

events.title: The Temptation in the Wilderness
events.description: After fasting 40 days, Jesus is tempted by the devil in the wilderness and overcomes using the Word of God.

events.title: The First Miracle at Cana
events.description: During a wedding feast, Jesus performs His first public miracle, turning water into wine.

events.title: The Encounter with Nicodemus
events.description: Jesus teaches the Pharisee Nicodemus about the need to be born again of the Spirit.

events.title: The Samaritan Woman at the Well
events.description: Jesus breaks social barriers by asking a Samaritan woman for water, revealing Himself to her as the Living Water and the Messiah.

events.title: The Sermon on the Mount
events.description: Jesus teaches the foundations of the Kingdom of God, delivering the Beatitudes and the Lord's Prayer.

events.title: The Miraculous Catch of Fish
events.description: After a night with no fish, Peter obeys Jesus and the nets break with abundance. Jesus calls them to be 'fishers of men'.

events.title: Healing the Paralytic Lowered Through the Roof
events.description: Four friends open a hole in the roof to reach Jesus, who forgives the man's sins and makes him walk.

events.title: Jairus's Daughter and the Bleeding Woman
events.description: On the way to resurrect the synagogue leader's daughter, Jesus heals a woman who touched the hem of His garment with faith.

events.title: Jesus Calms the Storm
events.description: The disciples despair during a fierce storm on the Sea of Galilee, but Jesus rebukes the winds and the sea with a word.

events.title: The Feeding of the 5,000
events.description: Jesus miraculously feeds a multitude of five thousand men with only five loaves of bread and two fish.

events.title: Jesus Walks on Water
events.description: During the night, Jesus goes out to the disciples walking on the sea. Peter attempts to go to Him, but sinks when he doubts.

events.title: The Transfiguration
events.description: Jesus is transfigured on the mountain before Peter, James, and John, revealing His glory while conversing with Moses and Elijah.

events.title: The Woman Caught in Adultery
events.description: Jesus confronts the woman's accusers, saying: 'Let him who is without sin among you be the first to throw a stone at her'.

events.title: The Parable of the Good Samaritan
events.description: To explain who our neighbor is, Jesus tells the story of the injured man on the road who is helped by a Samaritan.

events.title: The Parable of the Prodigal Son
events.description: Jesus illustrates the grace of God through the story of the rebellious son who returns to the arms of a loving father.

events.title: The Resurrection of Lazarus
events.description: Jesus weeps over His friend's death and resurrects him, calling him out of the tomb after four days of being buried.

events.title: The Encounter with Zacchaeus
events.description: The tax collector climbs a tree to see Jesus passing by. Jesus stays at his house, bringing salvation and repentance.

events.title: The Triumphal Entry
events.description: Jesus enters Jerusalem riding on a donkey, acclaimed by the crowds with palm branches and shouts of 'Hosanna'.

events.title: The Cleansing of the Temple
events.description: Consumed by zeal, Jesus drives out the money changers and merchants who made the House of God a den of thieves.

events.title: The Last Supper and Washing of Feet
events.description: Jesus washes the disciples' feet, institutes the New Covenant of the bread and the cup, and warns of Judas's betrayal.

events.title: Agony in Gethsemane and Arrest
events.description: Jesus prays in anguish in the garden until He sweats blood. He is betrayed with a kiss by Judas and arrested by the guards.

events.title: The Trial Before Pilate
events.description: Jesus is brought before the Roman governor Pontius Pilate, suffers the scourging, and the crowd chooses to release Barabbas.

events.title: The Crucifixion at Calvary
events.description: Jesus carries the cross and is crucified between two thieves. He utters His last words and gives up His spirit.

events.title: The Empty Tomb and Resurrection
events.description: The women find the tomb empty. Jesus resurrects victoriously on the third day and appears to Mary Magdalene.

events.title: The Road to Emmaus
events.description: The resurrected Christ walks with two disciples on the road and reveals the Scriptures, being recognized only in the breaking of the bread.

events.title: The Ascension into Heaven
events.description: After 40 days instructing the disciples, Jesus ascends gloriously into heaven before their eyes, promising to return.

events.title: The Day of Pentecost
events.description: The Holy Spirit is poured out on the apostles; Peter preaches and nearly three thousand people are baptized.

events.title: The Stoning of Stephen
events.description: Stephen, full of grace and power, becomes the first Christian martyr by being stoned in Jerusalem.

events.title: The Conversion of Saul
events.description: On the road to Damascus, the persecutor Saul has an encounter with the resurrected Christ and becomes the apostle Paul.

events.title: The Council of Jerusalem
events.description: The church leaders gather to decide that Gentile converts do not need to follow all Jewish laws.

events.title: Paul at the Areopagus in Athens
events.description: During his missionary journeys, Paul preaches to the Greek philosophers about the 'Unknown God'.

events.title: Persecution and Martyrdom
events.description: Emperor Nero blames the Christians for the great fire of Rome, unleashing severe persecutions where Peter and Paul are martyred.

events.title: The Destruction of Jerusalem
events.description: The Roman army, led by Titus, besieges Jerusalem and completely destroys the Second Temple, as Jesus had prophesied.
